survey: A cluster of branching corals on a group of rocks, standing on a flat green ground plane whose horizon sits about a third of the way up the card. A large pink coral grows up from the top of the central dark rock, with its branches spread mostly across the picture plane and facing the camera. A violet coral sits in front of it on the left and leans on the rock's left side. Orange corals stand behind on the left and right, partly hidden, and appear to grow from behind the rocks. Several low, rounded grey-blue rocks sit on the ground. Their tops show slightly from above, which matches a camera a little above the ground. The rocks overlap from front to back. A small red coral stands on the ground in front of the central rock. The ground meets the background along a level line, and every rock rests flat on it. The corals are organic shapes with no repeated rigid elements. Their surface dots are drawn as small round pits that shrink a little where the branches curve away, which is consistent with how those branches are lit and modelled.
